claims.claim: The design does not claim transactional exactly-once behavior across EventGraph, Work, Git, and GitHub.
claims.evidence: The scheduler section now defines deterministic attempt identities, reconcile-before-retry, conflict blocking, and effect idempotency while expressly rejecting a distributed-transaction claim.

claims.claim: The v1 service must not inherit or republish tracked credential-looking configuration found during checkpoint audit.
claims.evidence: The topology requires fresh mode-0600 configuration, forbids reading hive/loop/config.env, and makes a secret-safe diff/config audit an executable acceptance condition.

claims.claim: Cross-family review must identify the actually available independent provider rather than naming an unavailable provider.
claims.evidence: Packet v1.0.1 binds CFADA/CFAR to the eligible local Ollama/Qwen/Alibaba family; IADA remains explicitly non-substitutive.

residual_risks: GitHub effects are reconciled and idempotent but cannot be transactionally committed with local EventGraph and Work state.
The v1 scheduler is intentionally single-instance; multi-host leader election remains v2.
The demonstration supports one author family and one independent reviewer family.
The installed governance cache has a noncanonical bytecode extra; gate evidence binds exact source files and result artifacts instead of claiming manifest parity.
non_authorizations: No production deployment or CanOperate expansion.
No direct default-branch push, branch-protection change, or merge of demonstration PRs.
No mutation or reuse of Operation #86 or other consumed evidence.
No credential reuse, disclosure, or evidence fabrication.
No value allocation or residual-risk closure.
